title: Pseudo-Dionysius and Maximus Confessor Scholia
shelf_note: A Greek minuscule manuscript (Vatican) of the Celestial Hierarchy (ch. 15) with marginal scholia in majuscule, as the title says. No tradition or collections are set, so there is no shelf to contradict.
rights_flag: The scan carries a burned-in banner "Copyright © Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana / powered by AMLAD·NTT DATA" and a diagonal watermark "Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana ... ALL RIGHTS RESERVED". The work is medieval, but the image itself is under the library's reproduction terms and needs checking.
structure_note: The book-level counts disagree: pages_translated is 0 in structure but 378 in the field. The book has 47 printed backsteps and 38 repeats among only 183 'printed' numbers. This leaf shows no visible folio number, so these are probably folio or quire marks misread by the OCR, or text numerals taken as page numbers (O11), not a broken page order.

pages.layout: one column of minuscule with enlarged initials set out into the left margin; marginal scholia in small majuscule down the left margin and across the foot; a small faint scholion block at the lower right; a strip of the facing leaf's text at the right edge (correctly not transcribed)

tr_errors.english: the <unclear>incorruptible</unclear>, the sleepless, the unattached and the unpolluted, free from the addition of the gods
tr_errors.problem: Fluent English built on the misread lines. The leaf says 'free, unbound, unattached, pure of external addition, likening to the simplicity of the divine'. Gods 'shining toward us' are invented.

tr_errors.source: Ἡ μὲν ἀληθινὴ καὶ ἁπλῆ καὶ μονοειδὴς σοφία.
tr_errors.english: The true, simple and uniform **wisdom** is seated among the gods. It also clothes them with the encircling robe that bestows honours. It carries the gifts of the gods in heavenly shapes and instruments.
tr_errors.problem: An invented passage. The leaf's sentence is 'since the simple and manifold wisdom clothes the naked and gives them implements to carry, let us unfold the sacred garments and instruments of the heavenly minds'.

tr_errors.english: while we are the ones illuminated
tr_errors.problem: The image reads νοερῶς ἐλλαμπόμενον ('illuminated noerically'). The English invents 'we' and cuts the link to the noetic/noeric scholion keyed by the asterisk.

tr_errors.english: <note>original: ἀποπροσθέσεως; the phrase is obscure in this copy. It seems to mean that the angels are free from anything added from outside.</note>
tr_errors.problem: The note blames the manuscript ('obscure in this copy') for an OCR misread. The copy plainly reads τῶν ἐκτὸς προσθήκης.

tr_errors.problem: The note asserts a corruption in the manuscript that is really the OCR's. The leaf has the standard wording the note quotes.

missing.english: Where it is, in the sixteenth reading, in the seventh chapter.
missing.why: A 'reading' (ἀνάγνωσις) is a lection or section division of the manuscript. Without a gloss a general reader cannot tell what is being cross-referenced.

missing.english: In *On the Divine Names*, in the fourth chapter, on light, he spoke of this.
missing.why: The reader needs to be told that *On the Divine Names* is another Dionysian treatise, the one the scholion points back to.

book_verdict: The opening of the page and several key words are misread. The English turns these misreads into fluent invented theology ('wisdom is seated among the gods'), and two notes blame the manuscript for corruption that is really the OCR's. The scan also carries a Vatican copyright stamp.
